entities.name: Francesco Armellini Pantalassi de' Medici
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Francesco Armellini Pantalassi de' Medici (died January 18, 1528) was a prominent cardinal and financial administrator whose career at the heart of the Roman Curia epitomized the intricate fusion of ecclesiastical power and secular finance during the turbulent early 16th century. Though born Francesco Pantalassi in Perugia, he adopted the prestigious Medici name upon his adoption by Pope Leo X in 1517, a strategic elevation that cemented his influence within the papal court. His significance stems from his instrumental role in managing the fiscal affairs of two Medici popes, Leo X and Clement VII, navigating a period marked by escalating military expenditures and growing pressures from European powers, particularly during the Italian Wars.

Armellini's ascent began with his appointment as protonotary apostolic and later as cardinal-priest of San Callisto in 1517. Under Leo X, he became Cardinal Camerlengo of the Holy Roman Church, effectively controlling the Apostolic Chamber, the primary financial organ of the papacy. He implemented aggressive fiscal policies, including the sale of offices, the imposition of new taxes, and the vigorous collection of ecclesiastical revenues, aiming to replenish a treasury often depleted by warfare and lavish patronage. His financial acumen, though often perceived as ruthless, allowed the papacy to fund ambitious artistic projects and military campaigns, notably during the Italian Wars. He was instrumental in raising funds for the League of Cognac against Emperor Charles V, a move that ultimately backfired disastrously.
